subsystem.name: GenericRuntimeObjects
subsystem.responsibility: Runtime infrastructure cluster: a multi-level slot allocator feeding the model/scene loader, generic singly-linked list containers and node maintenance, the HUD penalty/warning message controller family (fines, warnings, stop-go penalties, disqualifications), a fixed-slot progress-bar event ring buffer, per-frame AI driver race-state/penalty enforcement, lap/split timing, and starting-grid assignment. Several owners are unknown; class boundaries here are DERIVED/GUESS proposals over validated function IR.

summary: Proposal for the generic_runtime_objects slice of Wave 3. The set clusters around: a multi-level allocator (0x4BB200) that builds a 4-byte header, a 384-byte payload of 32 x 12-byte slots, and two 12-byte-node lists (block list and slot list), used by the model/scene file loader (0x4B6C90); generic singly-linked list node removal by value (0x4BB6B0) and list destruction (0x4BF640) over a shared 4-dword control block and 12-byte nodes; a HUD penalty/warning message family sharing the same guard fields (this+0x0 penalty-state pointer, this+0x4 driver id, this+0x30 pending flag) in fine display (0x4BBA90), warning handler (0x4BBC60), stop-go penalty handler (0x4BBD60) and disqualification handler (0x4BC0E0), all resolving tokens through the message table (byte_5EC4C0 -> byte_5EC4CC) and rendering on dword_7CD204; a fixed-slot progress-bar event ring buffer (dword_8AAE64 pointer, dword_83EE60 count capped 1023, 432-byte stride, dbl_8AFEA0 time) written by 0x4BBD60/0x4BBF20/0x4BC0E0/0x4BC390 via ProgressBarEventEncode (0x4B33B0); per-frame AI driver race-state update (0x4BCCC0, owner AIDriverController) covering distance projection, pit-lane speed limits, corner-cut and wrong-way detection, and pit-selection through the dword_5EB978 state machine; lap/split timing (0x4BC390); grid alignment/jump-start validation (0x4BC9B0); racing-line mode reset guard (0x4BC240); snapshot field copies (0x4BC320/0x4BC330); a four-dword zeroer (0x4BF630); a conditional secondary-data destructor (0x4BB460); and starting-grid assignment for championship sessions (0x4BFF70). Ownership is UNKNOWN at the function-IR level for most members; classes here are DERIVED/GUESS proposals, not confirmed identities.

function_roles.role: Multi-level allocator setup on a __thiscall container: allocates a 4-byte header holding a pointer to a 384-byte payload block (32 slots x 12 bytes), registers the block as an in-use 12-byte node at the head of the block-level list (head this+0, tail this+4, back this+8, count this+0xC), then walks the block and chains one free 12-byte slot node per slot into the slot-level list (head this+0x10, tails this+0x14/0x18, count this+0x1C); returns the last allocated slot node for the caller ModelSceneFileLoader.

Secondary-data destructor: frees the allocation at this+0x4 through FreeWrapper_7bcf when non-null, then frees the object itself through the same wrapper when flag bit 0 of a2 is set; returns this. Called by ModelSceneFileLoader.

Singly-linked list node removal by value: walks from head this+0 through node+4 next links comparing each node's first dword to a2; on a match unlinks the node, maintains head this+0, second pointer this+4 and tail this+8, decrements count this+0xC, clears or honors the node flag byte at +8, frees the node's owned data via FreeWrapper_7bcf when flagged, frees the node itself, and returns 1.

HUD fine/penalty message display: gated on the pending flag this+0x30 and the penalty-state flag obj+0x32C8 (read through this+0); resolves the 'Fined US'/'Penalty' token and the driver name through the message table into byte_5EC4CC, formats the fine amount (CRTFtol) and renders via TextLineWrappingAndRendering; accumulates the fine total at this+0xA4.

HUD warning message display: gated on the pending-warning flag this+0x30, a non-null a2, and the penalty-state flag obj+0x32C8 (read through *this); resolves the 'Warning' token into byte_5EC4CC, conditionally replaces it with the a2 message, formats '%s %s' into a 192-byte buffer and renders it on the HUD; returns the flag read from this+0x30.

Stop-go penalty handler: gated on this+0x30; resolves 'Stop Go Penalty' plus driver name through the message table, renders to the HUD text line, records a ring-buffer penalty event (type 4, id 23) carrying driver id this+0x4 and session time, then dispatches the penalty to the vehicle object via sub_41A720.

Emits a progress-bar stage event (type 4, id 24) into the fixed-slot ring buffer via ProgressBarEventEncode with driver id this+0x4 and session time, advancing the write pointer by 432 and capping the count at 1023; returns the stage value at this+0x44.

Disqualification handler: when this+0x30 != 3, renders 'Disqualified: <driver>' on the HUD and logs a disqualification event (type 4, id 28) into the ring buffer, then dispatches via sub_41A940; the message path requires a driver-name a2 and a clear penalty-state flag obj+0x32C8. this+0x30 is only read, never written, so the routine cannot re-arm itself.

Per-frame racing-line mode guard: when the session-type global dword_7C56A4 is not qualifying (7), reads the object pointer at this+0, and if the object flag byte obj+0x344C is set resets the racing-line mode at this+0x60 from 2 to 1; returns the object pointer.

Snapshot field copy: reads the dword at this+0x2C, copies the float at this+0x68 into this+0x28, stores the dword into this+0x24 and returns it; used by multiplayer vehicle placement and netcomm slot-sync paths to preserve a current-state snapshot before an update.
Unconditional field copy: reads the int at this+0x24, writes it to this+0x2C and returns the copied value; invoked by MultiplayerVehiclePlacement and RestartGate.

Lap/split timing event processor: aborts early when the float at this+0xB0 exceeds 10.0, reads the event-type flag via FlagPropertyGetter(2048) from obj+0x32C8, routes on the event type (0/1/2) against the lap/sector state at this+0xC, computes a split-time delta from this+0x60/0x64, optionally writes encoded event data, allocates a ring-buffer slot, encodes a progress-bar event (type 4, id 8) and finalizes via LapCompletion.

Grid alignment / jump-start validator: dereferences this+0 to the vehicle float base, computes a velocity/acceleration magnitude squared (obj+0x34F8/0x34FC/0x3500) and orientation dot products; in penalty-check mode applies StopGoPenaltyHandler or DisqualificationHandler jump-start penalties when global dword_7CEF84 is set and the penalty-state flag obj+0x32C8 is not already 1; otherwise renders 'not lined up' status messages.

Per-frame AI driver race-state update (from MainGameTickUpdate): recomputes and wraps the driver's track distance projection, enforces pit-lane speed limits with stop-go penalties and monetary fines, detects corner cutting and wrong-way driving, manages cut-track/blue-flag penalty timers, and drives pit-entry selection based on nearby-vehicle proximity through the dword_5EB978 state machine.

Zero-initializes four consecutive dwords of a __thiscall object at this+0x0/0x4/0x8/0xC and returns this; a pure field writer used at object setup by AI driver count, filter-data loading and generic struct-init paths.

Destroys the singly-linked list rooted at this+0: for each node reads the flag byte at node+8 and the next pointer at node+4, frees the node payload (first dword) via FreeWrapper_7bcf when flagged, then frees the node; afterwards zeroes the four head dwords this+0..0xC and returns a value captured from sub_4BF730.

Starting-grid assignment for championship sessions (dword_7D0410 in 1..5): the qualifying path gathers per-driver qualifying position and time, sorts ascending by position, and writes grid position and time into 18624-byte-stride vehicle records; the non-qualifying path places the player (random when dword_7D0110 is zero) and fills the remaining vehicles sequentially, skipping the player grid.

classes.name: MultiLevelAllocator
classes.responsibility: Two-level slot allocator. Holds two singly-linked node lists over a 4-byte header whose single dword points to a 384-byte payload block split into 32 x 12-byte slots. The block list (head/tail/back/count) registers the payload block as an in-use node; the slot list (head, two tails, count) chains one free node per slot. Used by the model/scene file loader to grow its object pool.

classes.name: SecondaryDataOwner
classes.responsibility: Small owned-object wrapper holding a secondary allocation at this+0x4. Its destructor frees the secondary data and conditionally frees the object itself based on the delete-flag bit of its argument. The container class identity is unknown; this+0x4 is not merged with any other owner's this+0x4.

classes.name: SinglyLinkedList
classes.responsibility: Generic singly-linked list container with a four-dword control block (head/second/tail/count) and 12-byte nodes holding (data/value, next, flag byte). Supports value-based node removal and full destruction; node payload freeing is governed by the node flag byte.

classes.name: PenaltyWarningController
classes.responsibility: HUD message controller family for race penalties and warnings. All four handlers share the guard fields this+0x0 (penalty-state object pointer), this+0x4 (driver id) and this+0x30 (pending-message flag); they resolve localized tokens and the driver name through the message table into the shared byte_5EC4CC buffer, render to the HUD text line, record ring-buffer penalty events, and accumulate the fine total at this+0xA4.

classes.name: ProgressBarEventWriter
classes.responsibility: Writes progress-bar stage events into the fixed-slot event ring buffer (write pointer dword_8AAE64, count dword_83EE60 capped at 1023, 432-byte stride, session time dbl_8AFEA0) and returns the current stage value.

classes.name: RacingLineModeController
classes.responsibility: Per-frame guard that resets the racing-line display mode outside qualifying sessions: reads the object pointer at this+0, checks its flag byte obj+0x344C, and resets this+0x60 from mode 2 to mode 1.

classes.name: SnapshotFieldCopier
classes.responsibility: Small snapshot/field-copy helper on a __thiscall object: copies the dword state pair (this+0x24 <-> this+0x2C) and the float pair (this+0x68 -> this+0x28); used by multiplayer placement and netcomm slot-sync paths to preserve a current-state snapshot before an update.

classes.name: LapSplitEventProcessor
classes.responsibility: Processes lap/split timing events. Routes the event-type flag (read from the vehicle penalty-state field obj+0x32C8 via FlagPropertyGetter) against the current lap/sector state at this+0xC, computes split-time deltas from this+0x60/0x64, optionally writes encoded event data, records a progress-bar event into the ring buffer and finalizes the lap/split via LapCompletion.

classes.name: GridAlignmentValidator
classes.responsibility: Validates grid alignment and jump-start violations for a vehicle: dereferences this+0 to the vehicle float base, computes velocity/acceleration magnitude and orientation dot products, applies stop-go or disqualification jump-start penalties (gated by global dword_7CEF84 and the penalty-state flag obj+0x32C8), and renders 'not lined up' status messages.

classes.name: AIDriverRaceStateController
classes.responsibility: Per-frame AI driver race-state and penalty controller (owner AIDriverController, DERIVED per packet). Tracks the driver's wrapped track distance, enforces pit-lane speed limits (stop-go or monetary fine), detects corner cutting and wrong-way driving with accumulators and thresholds, manages cut-track/blue-flag timers, and drives pit-entry selection from nearby-vehicle proximity through the dword_5EB978 pit-selection state machine.

classes.name: Vehicle
classes.responsibility: Shared-layout proposal for the vehicle/object read through the penalty controllers and validators: carries the penalty-state flag at +0x32C8 (offset 13000, gates HUD penalty messages), a session/pit-lane flag at +0x344C, velocity/acceleration at +0x34F8..0x3500, orientation-matrix columns at +0x34C4/0x34D0/0x34DC, position at +0x34E0..0x34E8, and the vehicle data block pointer at +0x3AA8. Multiple owners read overlapping subsets, so this is a shared-layout grouping, not a confirmed single class.

classes.name: VehicleDataBlock
classes.responsibility: Track geometry / segment data block reached through the vehicle's +0x3AA8 pointer. Holds the segment direction vector (+0x0/4/8), position-referenced fields (+0x20/24/28), track half-widths (+0x68/6C), boundary vectors (+0xA4/A8/AC), a direction-block pointer (+0x110) and a further field (+0x12C). Referenced only by the AI driver race-state controller.

classes.name: TrackDirectionBlock
classes.responsibility: Direction vector block reached through VehicleDataBlock +0x110. Its three floats at +0x0/4/8 are used to project the wrong-way displacement during the wrong-way check.

classes.name: IntBlockZeroer
classes.responsibility: Zeroes the first four dwords of a __thiscall object and returns this. Used at setup time by AI driver count, filter-data loading and generic struct-init paths; the owner class is unknown.

classes.name: StartingGridAssigner
classes.responsibility: Assigns starting grid positions and times for championship sessions (dword_7D0410 in 1..5). The qualifying path gathers and sorts per-driver qualifying results (via 0x4C0260/0x4C02D0) then writes grid/time into 18624-byte-stride vehicle records; the non-qualifying path places the player from dword_7D0110 or a random draw and fills the remaining vehicles sequentially.

state_machines.name: PitSelectionStateMachine
states: considering (candidate recorded: blue-flag flag this+0xD4 and index this+0xD8)
waiting (pit-selection state dword_5EB978 advanced with events 1/2/3 on timer transitions)
enforced (blue-flag timer this+0xDC exceeds 30 with penalties enabled: stop-go applied, timer reset)

transitions.condition: a mode-specific rival candidate qualifies by wrapped track-distance proximity within the lateral time window
no candidate, recorded index changed, or mode != 7 with a nonzero timer: ClearPitSelectionFlags(5) via sub_41B910
pit-selection state machine (dword_5EB978) advanced via sub_41B3C0 with events 1/2/3 at timer 0/10/20 seconds
blue-flag timer this+0xDC exceeds 30 and dword_7CEF84 set: stop-go penalty + message via sub_41A720, timer reset
external writer sets this+0x30 to 3 (this+0x30 is only read, never written, in 0x4BC0E0; the writer is elsewhere)

state_machines.name: CornerCutTrackingStateMachine
states: tracking (lateral offset > 2.5: lap/segment/projection snapshotted, accumulators reset, flag set)
violated (cut depth > 1.75 with repeat count this+0xD0 > 1 or depth > 2.75, penalties enabled)

transitions.condition: lateral offset exceeds 2.5: snapshot lap/segment/projection, reset accumulators, set in-progress flag
corner-cut flag this+0xB4 set and lateral offset below 1.0
cut depth this+0xCC > 1.75 and (cut count this+0xD0 > 1 or depth > 2.75) and dword_7CEF84 set: stop-go 10s or warning via WarningHandler
corner-cut tracking not enabled (sub_4BC340 returns false): clear the in-progress flag

interfaces.name: IProgressBarEventWriter
interfaces.purpose: Contract for writing progress-bar/penalty/lap events into the fixed-slot ring buffer (write pointer dword_8AAE64, count dword_83EE60 capped at 1023, 432-byte stride, session time from dbl_8AFEA0) through ProgressBarEventEncode (0x4B33B0). Event payload: float delta at +8, event-type word at +12, parameter word at +14.

interfaces.name: IHudMessageRenderer
interfaces.purpose: Shared HUD message rendering pattern: resolves a localization token and the driver name through the message string table (byte_5EC4C0) into the shared buffer byte_5EC4CC, formats '%s %s' / '%s%d %s' with overflow checking, and renders through TextLineWrappingAndRendering on the resource at dword_7CD204.

interfaces.name: IVehiclePenaltyDispatch
interfaces.purpose: Dispatch of a penalty/DQ decision to the vehicle object with the driver-name string as payload: stop-go and ignored-blue-flag penalties go through sub_41A720, disqualification through sub_41A940.

compatibility_contracts.name: ProgressBarEventRingBufferContract
compatibility_contracts.description: A fixed-slot event ring buffer is exposed through globals: write pointer dword_8AAE64, slot count dword_83EE60 capped at 1023, 432-byte stride per entry, session time from dbl_8AFEA0. Events are encoded via ProgressBarEventEncode (0x4B33B0) with type 4 and ids 23 (stop-go penalty), 24 (progress stage), 8 (lap split) and 28 (disqualification); the payload stores a float delta at +8, an event-type word at +12 and a parameter word at +14.

compatibility_contracts.name: PenaltyStateFlagContract
compatibility_contracts.description: The penalty-state flag at obj+0x32C8 (byte offset 13000 of the penalty-state/vehicle object, read through the controller's this+0) gates every HUD penalty/warning message: a clear flag permits the message; a set flag (value 1 blocks jump-start re-penalty) suppresses it. The same flag selects the lap/split event type via FlagPropertyGetter bit 2048.

compatibility_contracts.name: PenaltiesEnabledContract
compatibility_contracts.description: Global dword_7CEF84 is the master switch for applying race penalties: stop-go penalties, monetary fines, corner-cut and wrong-way penalties and blue-flag enforcement all check it before acting. A replacement must preserve this gate to reproduce penalty behavior.

compatibility_contracts.name: SessionTypeContract
compatibility_contracts.description: Global dword_7C56A4 encodes the session type; value 7 (qualifying) disables racing-line reset and selects fixed stop-go penalties instead of fines, while dword_7C56A8 != 5 gates pit-selection logic. Threshold comparisons and branch meanings are DERIVED from branch structure, not named constants.

compatibility_contracts.name: VehicleRecordStrideContract
compatibility_contracts.description: Vehicle records are laid out at 18624-byte stride (count from dword_5C329C; bases include unk_5EC6D0, unk_5F0CF8, unk_5F070C, unk_5F0734). Grid position is written at dword index 9, qualifying time as float at index 10, and the player grid at byte offset 16472 (with sentinel -1082130432 at 16476) on the vehicle at dword_7C54E8. These offsets are IDB-normalized reads from 0x4BFF70.

compatibility_contracts.name: ChampionshipGridGateContract
compatibility_contracts.description: Grid assignment runs only when dword_7D0410 (championship mode) is in 1..5. The qualifying-session path runs when dword_7D0110 equals a second display/session field (spelled dword_7D011C in raw source, absent from the packet global list); otherwise the random/sequential placement path runs.

compatibility_contracts.name: MultiLevelAllocationLayoutContract
compatibility_contracts.description: The multi-level allocator exposes: a 4-byte header whose single dword points to a 384-byte payload block split into 32 x 12-byte slots; 12-byte nodes holding (data pointer, next pointer, flag byte); a block list (head this+0, tail this+4, back this+8, count this+0xC) and a slot list (head this+0x10, tails this+0x14/0x18, count this+0x1C). Block nodes are marked in-use (flag 1), slot nodes free (flag 0).

compatibility_contracts.name: MessageStringTableContract
compatibility_contracts.description: Localized message tokens are resolved through the string table at byte_5EC4C0 into the shared buffer byte_5EC4CC: aFinedUs (0x5D255C), aPenalty (0x5D2548), aWarning (0x5D2568), aStopGoPenalty (0x5D2574), aDisqualified (0x5D2588), aNotLinedUp (0x5D2598), aWrongWay (0x5D25B0), aLapWillNotCoun (0x5D25BC), plus driver names. Rendered through TextLineWrappingAndRendering on dword_7CD204; format strings '%s %s' and '%s%d %s' via StringFormatWithBufferOverflowCheck.

unresolved: The owners of most functions are UNKNOWN at the function-IR level; the class grouping above is a DERIVED/GUESS proposal, not a confirmed identity.
The 12-byte node flag-byte semantics (in-use vs free) and the two-list (block list + slot list) design of the multi-level allocator are not documented in the packet.
0x4BB460's this+0x4 is a secondary data pointer, distinct from MultiLevelAllocator's this+0x4 (block-list tail); per rule 8 the equal offset is not merged across owners.
The role of the SinglyLinkedList second pointer at this+0x4 (head/cursor/tail ambiguity) is not fully determined; only the head this+0 and tail this+0x8 show clear behavior in 0x4BB6B0.
Why 0x4BB6B0 frees the node's data directly while its structural twin 0x4BA830 performs an EmptyStub_0170() call is unresolved.
The pending-message flag this+0x30 is only read by the penalty/warning handlers (0x4BBA90/0x4BBC60/0x4BBD60/0x4BC0E0); the writer that sets it (including the value 3 for 'disqualified') is elsewhere.
Globals aSS_2 (0x5C5D30) and aSDS (0x5D2554) are packet-listed as referenced but appear nowhere in the raw decompiled bodies; their roles are not verifiable.
The meaning of the byte_7D0B10 flag (which message flavor 'Fined US' vs 'Penalty' is emitted) is not documented inside the function.
The obj+0x32C8 penalty-state flag versus driver-name-field binding is taken from the skeleton fill, not from the raw function code.
The StopGoPenaltyHandler third-argument literal 10 and the render-call literals (3, 16909060) have no named meaning in the raw source.
dbl_59EB48 is packet-listed for 0x4BC390 but the raw source compares the literal 10.0, so the ride-height-threshold binding is not verifiable.
The default (unlisted) switch case of the 0x4BC390 event-type selector falls through to sub_4BC340 with no state check; the meaning of a2 values outside 0..2 is unstated.

The 0x4BC9B0 threshold literals (1.0, 5.0625, 1.5, 0.75, 3.0625, 1.25, 0.85, 225.0, 400.0) have no named constants in the raw source; the flt_ constants packet-listed for it are not visible in the raw body.

In 0x4BCCC0 the packet-listed callees FloatRangeIndexLookup (0x4D7C10) and AISessionModeTransition (0x4193A0) are not visible in the raw body and cannot be placed; the many flt_/dbl_ float constants and dword_8AD264 are likely folded into FPU immediates by Hex-Rays.

In 0x4BCCC0 the field base expressions (obj / *(obj+0x3AA8) / *(*(obj+0x3AA8)+0x110)) are IDB-normalized; their correspondence to the raw pointer arithmetic (v3/v5/v34) is approximate. The obj+0x344C read is treated as the pit-lane/session flag at context+13388, conflicting with an existing-analysis label ('segment normal'); the raw reading was favored.
The obj+0x34F8/0x34FC/0x3500 field refs in 0x4BCCC0 have no clear anchor in the decompiled source and are left unresolved, though the same offsets are used as velocity/acceleration in 0x4BC9B0.
The 0x4BCCC0 this+0x60 guard (guard:1, != 2) is tied to cut-track / pit-proximity flag semantics only approximately.
At the ring-buffer cap (dword_83EE60 >= 1023) the write pointer is reused instead of advancing; the semantics of the 1023 cap are unresolved.
The purpose and side effects of sub_4BF730 (called first by 0x4BF640, its return passed through) are unknown.
In 0x4BFF70 the qualifying/random branch compares dword_7D0110 against a second display/session field spelled dword_7D011C in the raw source, which is absent from the packet global list.
The exact VEH field semantics behind the unk_5F070C and unk_5F0734 writes (grid position vs qualifying time) follow the existing analysis and are not independently confirmed.
The event ids/type-4 constants and the 432-byte ring-buffer stride have no in-packet documentation.
Semantics of the a3 flag in 0x4BC9B0 (emit 'not lined up' status message) are inferred, not proven; exact UI/status semantics unknown.
The vehicle float magnitude-squared reading of obj+0x34F8/0x34FC/0x3500 in 0x4BC9B0 is labeled velocity/acceleration by the fill; the transform is not proven.
